While he is still a formidable villain who attempts to kill Batman, he is far more easier to reason with than usual, while having many instances of being sincerelyAffably Evil.He is immensely respectful and sincere in wanting to help the Weeper, which is a contrast to the comics where his team-up with the latter's son andsuccessorduring the Bronze AgeJustice League of Americastory "Crisis on Earth-S", had him insulting and dismissive towards him the whole time.He appears to genuinely respect Batman, leading up to their team-up where he muses they could have been friends in another universe. Where he also, rather begrudgingly, saved a kid's life.His usualabusivebehavior towards Harley is mostly absent, aside from a silly instance of him using powers to mute her voice. He is immensely respectful and sincere in wanting to help the Weeper, which is a contrast to the comics where his team-up with the latter's son andsuccessorduring the Bronze AgeJustice League of Americastory "Crisis on Earth-S", had him insulting and dismissive towards him the whole time. He appears to genuinely respect Batman, leading up to their team-up where he muses they could have been friends in another universe. Where he also, rather begrudgingly, saved a kid's life. His usualabusivebehavior towards Harley is mostly absent, aside from a silly instance of him using powers to mute her voice.

characters.name: Mongul
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: The evil ruler of War World, he originally sought to use Jonah Hex as a way to beat Batman once and for all. When that failed, he brought a War Moon to Earth in an attempt to destroy the world, while also humoring its heroes and villains with a race to see if he'd do it. Adaptational Wimp: Batman and Jonah Hex went up against him in this show and survived. In the comics, Mongul is roughly equal to Superman in strength, and would have crushed them both easily. Blood Sport: He holds gladiator style matches where participants are forced to fight to death. Bond Villain Stupidity: Who would teleport losing racers to a cell rather than let them die? He does ensure the prisoners are separated from their various tools and trapped behind forcefields, but he foolishly never considered that Batman and Green Arrow would anticipate that. Composite Character: Is a mix of both Monguls, being the ruler of Warworld like the original, but the rivalry with Mongal comes from his son.

characters.name: Black Manta
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Black Manta is a criminal from the surface world who frequently clashes with AQUAMAN. Animal Motifs: The manta, of course. Arch-Enemy: Shares the same burning hatred for AQUAMAN as any other of his counterparts. Arm Cannon: He has two. Color Character:BlackManta.

characters.name: Clock King
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: The first villain to appear inThe Brave and the Bold, Clock King has simple goals in life: assemble a clock-themed group of henchmen in a clock-themed secret lair, construct elaborate clock-themed traps and/or weapons, and use them to rob banks and/or kill Batman. Adaptational Dumbass: This version never actually shows off his trademarkClock Kingprecision planning. Adaptational Wimp: He has neither theClock Kingplanning abilities, nor theTime Masterpowers. He's basically just a normal guy wearing a silly clock-themed costume. Badass Cape: A fancy-looking one with a fur trim. Badass Normal: He's actually pretty ripped. He was once shown lifting weights in prison.

characters.name: Doctor Sivana
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A mad scientist who plagues Fawcett City with his demented schemes, with assistance from his children, requiring the intervention of Captain Marvel. Arch-Enemy: To Captain Marvel. Bald of Evil: Not a hair on his head, and evil as they come. Daddy's Little Villain: His children, Thaddeus Junior and Georgia, help out in his mad schemes. Eviler than Thou: Pulls this on Black Adam, duping the former Champion into defeating Captain Marvel and the Wizard for him and then stealing his powers. Later ends up on the receiving end from Mister Mind.

characters.name: Kanjar Ro
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A power-hungry space-pirate andArch-Enemyof the Blue Beetle. Adaptational Curves: Compared to his often-slender comic book counterpart. Arch-Enemy: Of a previous wielder of the Blue Beetle scarab before it came into the possession of Dan Garrett. Badass Normal: He doesn't seem to possess any powers other than standard hand-to-hand combat and instead relies on advanced technology and cunning. Omnicidal Maniac: Several of his plans have involved the attempted destruction of planets.

characters.name: Lex Luthor
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: To Superman, naturally. The Bad Guy Wins: After he successfully defeats Batman in the episode "Triumvirate of Terror". Bald of Evil: Like most versions of the character, he is a bald superillain. Composite Character: He shares the rotund build and openly detested reputation of his classic self, but also uses aPowered Armorlike his modern self does. Curb-Stomp Battle: Delivers one when he breaks into the Batcave, with hisPower Armordesigned to fight Superman proving more than a match for anything Batman has.

characters.name: Two-Face
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Once Gotham City's DA Harvey Dent, his face got scarred andhis personality was split: one half good, one half evil. His coin decides what the two personalities do. Batman hopes he can be reformed because Harvey was a good friend of Bruce Wayne's. Combat Pragmatist: Fair's good... Butgunsare better! Enemy Mine: Manages to be both the guest hero and the villain of hisdebut teaserafter hismooksquestion the results of sparing Batman after a coin toss. Even Evil Has Standards: Hewillstay true to his coin toss. If it says a person lives, they live. Eviler than Thou: Lost to Matches Malone.Actually Batman withAmnesia.

characters.name: Baby Face
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Alfonso Vincenzo Giuseppe Face is a ruthless gangster with the face of a young child, but a manly voice of Edward G. Robinson. Though when he is defeated he whines like a baby, and he also wears diapers. Berserk Button: Don't disrespect his gal. Canon Immigrant: He was created for the series, but was later brought into the comics inHarley Quinn (2016)#70 Even Evil Has Loved Ones: He'll quite happily dish out the hurt to our heroes or indeed any innocentRed Shirt, but he genuinely loves Miss Manface and hasmade an honest woman of herby the time of "Night of the Huntress". Expy: Quite similar to Baby Doll fromBatman: The Animated Serieswith both being villains who suffer from conditions that make themlook like children, although Baby Face is just aTiny-Headed Behemoth. Both also get into anUnholy Matrimonywith another villain.

characters.name: The Brain
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A genius with his mind stuck in a robotic body, the Brain uses his intellect to get back at the world by committing heinous crimes. Adaptational Badass: Minor case. In the comics he poses no physical threat as his body has no means of defense. Here, while still one of the weaker characters, he can produce weapons to defend himself. Brain in a Jar: Naturally. French Jerk: He is French, as in the original comics, and the series even gives him a French accent. Good Colors, Evil Colors: His brain is, for some unexplained reason,green, whilehis robotic body is black and his "eyes" and "mouth" are red.

characters.name: The Cavalier
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A criminal who has based himself on a 17th century swordsman. Affably Evil: He's fairly polite and well-spoken for a criminal. He even compliments Green Arrow when the latter disguises himself as Batman to make up for him being temporarily crippled, citing that he appreciates the Caped Crusader apparently picking up more noble weaponry. Recurring Character: After his debut appearance in the episode "The Eyes of Despero", he would later go on to make three additional episode appearances in the episodes "A Bat Divided" (hanging out at the villains bar before he is zapped by a tazer from Batman), "Night of the Batmen" (as one of the many criminals in Gotham who sees Batman's absence from crimefighting as his opportunity to commit crimes), and "Bold Beginnings" (in which he distracts Batman and Green Arrow by using Ruby Ryder's hostage situation as his opportunity to reveal that Ruby Rider never needed to be saved at all before her true colors are soon revealed) . Ye Olde Butcherede Englishe: Possibly the Cavalier's most heinous of crimes is his constant use of mangled faux-Elizabeathan English. It gets aLampshade Hangingfrom Batman in one appearance.Batman:(after having just heard the Cavalier speak)Somewhere, Shakespeare is spinning in his grave.

characters.name: Mr. Freeze
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A cold supervillain with an icy temperament. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In the first season, he was drawn based on his original appearance as Mr. Zero. Season 2 onwards gives him a moreRay Gun Gothicaesthetic, similar to George Sanders’ costume fromBatman (1966). Early-Installment Weirdness: Going with the above trope, his first appearance called him “Mr. Zero”. Though given Bat-Mite was the only one to refer to him as such, it was likely his fanboy OCD kicking in. Mythology Gag: When he’sSuddenly Voicedin Season 3, his portrayal draws heavily from Otto Preminger’s portrayal inBatman (1966), even having “Wild” as aCatchphrase. Not-So-Harmless Villain: While he’s based on the character back when he was a Z-lister, he still captures three of Batman’s allies and comes very close to finishing up a plan to freeze Gotham.

characters.name: Owlman
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Exactly who Owlman is has never been revealed, but what we do know is that he's as evil as Batman is good.Exactlyas evil. Batman's counterpart in anAlternate Universe, Owlman led a team of other such evil twins against the heroes of his world, and eventually defeated and imprisoned all but one. Now, with his Earth subjugated by the Injustice Syndicate, Owlman's sights are set on the conquest of other worlds. Animal Motifs: Owls, right down to a gadget that includes nightvision. Costume Copycat: He steals an earlier version of Batman's outfit, and uses it to ruin Batman's reputation. Face Framed in Shadow: Very noticeably, when Batman takes his costume for himself, Owlman's face remains obscured while he's sitting in the Batcave's holding cell. No Name Given: His identity is never revealed, though if he's anything like his comic version, it's Thomas Wayne Junior.

characters.name: Ra's al Ghul
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A well-intentioned villain who wants to protect nature... by destroying human civilization. Despite his views on nature, he's rather old fashioned when it comes to his daughter Talia, feeling that a woman is incapable of succeeding him. Affectionate Nickname: Like other versions, he calls Batman by the title "Detective". Beard of Evil: Sports his traditional dual-horned beard. Disney Villain Death: Appears to be the case at the end of "Crisis: 22,300 Miles Above Earth!". Fights Like a Normal: His only power is his immortality, wherein he otherwise fights like a normal butveryskilled human.

characters.name: Solomon Grundy
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Badass in a Nice Suit: Unlike the usual depiction of the character, this Grundy sports a full suit three piece suit, complete with tie and pocket square and topped off with a snazzy fedora. This is justified as this version is more overtly a gangster. Intelligible Unintelligible: As the middle of his mouth is stitched shut, Grundy only communicates via slurred grumbling. The only characters who can understand him are his henchman Weasel, who translates his orders to other goons, and Killer Croc Our Zombies Are Different: Cyrus Gold was resurrected by a mix of a greed curse and residual magic in a swamp, he's also more intelligent than the average walking dead man, enough to run a small organized crime unit, even if he's supposedly less intelligent than his original self.

characters.name: Talia al Ghul
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Ra's al Ghul's daughter, she wants to be his heir and feels threatened by his interest in Robin. So far she doesn't appear to return Robin's attraction to her. Age Lift: Her exact age isn't specified, but it's hinted she's much closer to Robin's age than Batman's in this continuity. Daddy's Little Villain: Lacks theinnocencesome of her other incarnations have, though that doesn't make her totally loyal to Ra's. The fact that her dad prefers a male heir may have something to do with it. Dating Catwoman: Robin washopingfor this, but is quickly shot down, though it's because she's only interested in Batman. Dual Wielding: She dual-wields a pair of knives in a fight.

characters.name: Black Adam
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A former champion of the wizard Shazam, five thousand years ago. Black Adam turned against the wizard, and was banished into the depths of space, until Doctor Sivana managed to summon him back to Earth. Evil Sounds Deep: He has a deep voice. Fallen Hero: He became corrupted by his power, and tried to take over the world, and so the Wizard banished him to "the furthest star". Flying Brick: Black Adam has all of Captain Marvel's power, and absolutelynoneof his kindness or compassion. Adam is one foe Batman iscompletely outclassedby. Hair-Trigger Temper: Just generally irritable. Much of Sivana's partnership with him is keeping Adam calm long enough to get what he wants, before Adam decides to tear his head off.

characters.name: Black Mask
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A ruthless Gotham mafioso with an odd fixation on masks, Black Mask leads his gang, the False Face Society, in a series of violent acts to take over the city. Adaptational Badass: The Black Mask in the comics was usually of average build and not much of a brawler; here, he's absolutely shredded and has some decent fighting skills. Bad Boss: He eventually tries to have his henchmen executed by the Bat-Bots once he deems them useless to his plans. Creepy Monotone: He speaks in a forced, strained monotone voice as if constantly making an active effort to restrain himself. Faux Affably Evil: He's superficially polite, but has no regard for the wellbeing of others.

characters.name: Blockbuster
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: While he simply appears to be a scrawny little punk, whenever Mark Desmond ingests the right chemicals, he becomes the super-strong Blockbuster, though his intelligence takes a hit when he does. Desmond's crimes are fuelled by the need for more funds. Chemicals don't come cheap, after all. Adaptational Villainy: The comics Blockbuster was only a villain because of his loyalty to his older brother Roland. This version is evil of his own free will. Adapted Out: Absolutely no mention of Bruce Wayne saving his life like in the comics is mentioned. Age Lift: Much,muchyounger than either of his comics counterparts. Composite Character: HeisMark Desmond, but being a criminal of his own accord comes from the second Blockbuster, his brother Roland.

characters.name: The Calculator
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Adaptation Name Change: In the comics, the Calculator's real name Noah Kuttler but here in the cartoon his name is Myron. Bald of Evil: He's a supervillain with a combover. Basement Dweller: He still lives in his mom's basement, which is the first place Huntress looks for him. Fat Bastard: He's a chubby, slovenly nerd who doesn't even wear pants at work, and that work is tattling for supervillains. Information Broker: For supervillains, he supplies knowledge on what superhero's doing what, in exchange for money.

characters.name: Catman
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Thomas Blake was world renowned for capturing wild cats. However, Blake became bored with hunting and had wasted his vast fortune. He became a thief called Catman. Catman's costume made from an ancient African cloth that is rumored to give its wearer nine lives. Nonetheless, Catman was accused of stealing the cat theme taken up by Catwoman. Animal Motifs: Cats, although not quite to the same extreme as Catwoman. Animal-Themed Superbeing: Wears a cat-like costume and supposedly has nine lives. Auction of Evil: In "Legends of the Dark Mite!", Catman illegally auctioned a rare Sumatran tiger to the highest bidder. Spear Counterpart: To Catwoman.

characters.name: The Cheetah
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Animal-Themed Superbeing: Type I. Arch-Enemy: One ofWonder Woman's main opponents. The Bad Guy Wins: After her plan to already be inside the Fortress of Solitude first without Superman knowing before she reveals herself to the man of steel himself which leads to her revealing to him she's wearing a magic based amulet around her neck (that both powers her up and exploits his weakness to magic) as well as wearing kryponite laced nail polish, both which makes Superman vulnerable to being defeated by Cheetah with little difficulty. Composite Character: Of herself. Even if her real name is never mentioned, her looks and personality correspond to Priscilla Rich, theGolden AgeCheetah, while her strength and abilities seem to have a magical origin, like the third Cheetah, Barbara Ann Minerva. Curb-Stomp Battle: Gives one to Superman after shegets an amulet than enhances her powers, and covers her claws with kryptonite.

characters.name: Chemo
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: A Kaiju sized pile of toxic waste. Dumb Muscle: Chemo has no brain of its own, and is either just lashing out in a mindless rage or is being directed by someone else. Poisonous Person: Batman accidentally catches a face full of Chemo's goop, and catches a near fatal case of "bilge". Defeating Chemo also has the problem that its substances are pure poison, and requires clean-up afterward if spilled. Shout-Out: Perhaps fitting for a nuclear monster, it reuses the sound ofthekaiju,Godzilla. The Voiceless: Roaring and screeching, but no voice.

characters.name: Crazy Quilt
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: An ex-painter who leads a double life as a master thief, he is blinded during a battle with Batman and Robin. While in prison, he volunteers for an experimental procedure that would restore his vision. There is a side-effect, however: Even though he can see, he can only see in blinding, disorienting colors. Crazy-Quilt's wears a helmet that allows him to hypnotize his victims using flashing lights of various colors. It can also project lethal laser beams, blinding lights, and functions as artificial eyes since his own eyes no longer function; the lenses feed their input signal straight into his brain. Arch-Enemy: To Robin. Energy Weapon: He shoots laser beams out of his helmet. Eye Scream: Quilt catches an eyeful of his own lasers. It doesn't completely blind him, but his eyesight's so badly damaged he might as well be. It's Personal: His motivation.

characters.name: Creature King
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: An alien despot obsessed with conquering the universe, Creature King first appears in the episode "Bold Beginnings!" during the teaser with a mind control helmet which he uses on several astrodactyls and moon apes. Batman later knocks him out, making the mind control helmet fall off his head in the process. Aliens Are Bastards: Oh yes very much so. Berserk Button: After he realizes Jan and Jace know what he's up to, he is not happy about it and sends his pet wyvern after the two. Bizarre Alien Biology: The Creature King himself who is no taller than a dwarf, has an appearance like that of a goblin (not to mention having pointy ears like one), and has fangs similar to vampire fangs. Hoist by His Own Petard: After his mind control is destroyed, his creature minions (including a maroon hodag with dark blue spikes, a red three eyed slug, and a metallic blue colored lava monster) get their long overdue revenge on their former master.

characters.name: Crimson Cloak
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A mysterious being haunting Batman, presumed to be the ghost of Sam Scarlett. Canon Character All Along:At first glance, Crimson Cloak appears to be just an exclusiveCanon Foreignervillain created for this movie, but in reality, it is Clayface in disguise under another identity. The Heavy:He appears as theBig BadofScooby-Doo! & Batman: The Brave and the Boldfrom the beginning, but he is actually working for The Riddler. Tragic Monster:Clayface did very little out of genuine malice, instead acting on the Riddler's orders in exchange for the cure to averyhorrifying degenerative disease.Daphne even openly says she feels sorry for him as he's carted off.

characters.name: Despero
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Adaptational Dye-Job: Despero's skin is usually red, while here he's purple. Adaptational Nice Guy: While he's still aGalactic Conqueror, he appears to prefer enslaving populations while they still remain alive. Bald of Evil: He's an evil alien, and completely bald. The Chessmaster: He manages to trick Batman and the Green Lanterns into fighting an illusion of himself while his real self successfully takes over Mogo while the heroes were distracted. Disproportionate Retribution: In the teaser for "Duel of the Double Crossers!" he has no problem with destroying a few cars, a stone monument, and a building. He also blew up a truck full of oil after being sent flying from an electricity blast from Black Lightning.

characters.name: Doctor Double X
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A man with a very literal split personality. Simon Ecks commits crimes in order to drain enough energy that he can give his more brutish other side a physical body of his own. Adaptation Origin Connection: Double X is the cause of Firestorm's origins here, since it's his attack on a power plant that fuses Ronnie Raymond and Jason Rusch. (In the comics, it was the result of the unscrupulous anti-nuclear protestor Eddie Earhart — a false mentor to Ronnie — sabotaging a nuclear facility that Martin Stein managed.) Divergent Character Evolution: Doctor X and Double X looked identical in the comics. Here, Double X is much taller and more muscular. Evil Counterpart: To Firestorm. Both are two people technically stuck in the one body, one a scrawny nerd, the other a towering thug. The difference is that Firestorm's components learn to get along and work together. The Simons just hate each other. Evil Sounds Deep: Not so much with Simon, whose voice is more nasal than most of Perlman's usual roles. Double X's voice is a bit deeper than his, though.

characters.name: Felix Faust
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Ambiguously Bi: While he flirts with Katrina, he doesn't seem to mind the reveal that Batman was in Katrina's body. Lean and Mean: He is skinny compared to most of the villains in the show. This Cannot Be!: His reaction when he believes Batman can do magic.

characters.name: Fun Haus
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: Red Tornado describes several of his crimes, including felony robbery, assault, parole violation, and jaywalking. Canon Foreigner: He was created for this show. Expy: He's based on Jack Nimball, the second Toyman, right down to wearing a similarly colored jester costume. Mythology Gag: He carries a toy version ofBaby Doll.

characters.name: Harley Quinn
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A psychiatrist who worked at Arkham Asylum untilshe met the Joker and grew to love him, eventually becoming his accomplice and on-off sidekick. Harley is seen with the Joker at the antiques museum in "Emperor Joker!" when he is about to steal his memorabilia until Batman shows up. While both the Dark Knight and the Clown Prince of Crime fight each other, Bat-Mite comes along and falls for her. When Bat-Miteaccidentally gives all his powers to the Joker in his attempt to help Batman, things start going to hell when the Joker recreates the universe in his own image and uses the Dark Knight as a cosmic punching bag by killing him repeatedly and bringing himBack from the Deadeach time. At the same time, both she and Bat-Mite question their faith in their heroes, since the latter care more about each other, and the former wonder if they'd be "better off without [them]". All Women Love Shoes: She wears her high heels in this one. Bash Brothers: A rare case when she and Bat-Mite work together to stop Joker-Mite from killing off Batman, even whenusing her title cards as weapons. Blowing a Raspberry: She does this to one of the Joker's henchmen, even though she is rendered mute. Carry a Big Stick: Even when she isDeliberately Monochrome, she never forgets that she is not afraid to use a mallet.

characters.name: The Injustice Syndicate
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: The greatest criminals of another Earth, the Crime Society assist Owlman in his villainous deeds. Adaptation Name Change: They are based on theCrimeSyndicate from the comics. Adapted Out: While based on the Crime Syndicate, the Injustice Syndicate isn't shown to have Ultraman, Superwoman, Power Ring or Johnny Quick as members, with Batman's counterpart Owlman being the only member from the source material to be represented. Ultraman and Superwoman's absences are somewhat understandable, as the team appeared before Superman and Wonder Woman's restrictions from use were resolved. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Silver Cyclone, Red Tornado'sEvil Doppelgänger, is an android supervillain who is not only in league with Owlman to conquer several alternate Earths, but also has a genocidal hatred of all organic life, his teammates included, that he is willing to wipe out all life of his own planet to rule it alone. Color Character:BlueBowman,ScarletScarab, andSilverCyclone.

characters.name: Jarvis Kord
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: The uncle of Ted Kord, the former Blue Beetle. Initially appearing as a friend to Jaime Reyes, Ted's successor, Jarvis turns out to be hiding sinister motives. Beard of Evil: A major distinction between him and the genuinely heroic Ted is his beard. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He initially pretends to be a nice, cheerful guy, but he uses Jaime as a pawn in his plan. He had previously done the same with Ted. Composite Character: With Max Lord, given both that his voice actor Tim Matheson voiced Lord inJustice Leagueand that much like Lord in the comics, this version of Jarvis is responsible for the death of Ted. Evil Uncle: And one who actuallysucceededin killing his nephew, Ted “Blue Beetle” Kord.

characters.name: Joe Chill
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Once a lowly street hood, working for Gotham's biggest crime lord, Lew Moxon, a young Joe Chill was desperate to make amends for screwing up a job, and on his boss's orders went after one Thomas Wayne, and in doing so helped create the Caped Crusader. Accidental Murder: Killing Thomas Wayne was intentional. Killing Martha wasn't. Alas, Poor Villain: He murdered the Waynes and remained an unrepentant criminal for his entire life but his final moments can evoke some sympathy. After Batman confronts him, beats him down, and reveals that he was the young son of the couple that Chill murdered, Joe Chill became so distraught that he ran out and told the other villains that he was the one who created Batman to try to get their help... only for them to mercilessly attack him for creating the hero who locks them up night after night. After that, Batman finally shows up to save him and in the struggle, part of the building is destroyed with debris falling on top of Chill, fatally wounding him. In his final moments, Joe Chill manages to share some parting words with Batman, acknowledging that Batman had gotten him in the end, and finally accepts what had happened to him in the end was fitting. Create Your Own Hero: His killing of Bruce Wayne's parents is what led to Bruce WaynebecomingBatman. Karma Houdini Warranty: He killed the Waynes and ran off into the night, evading Bruce Wayne's attempts to find out who he was for years, while becoming a highly successful weapons dealer. Had the Spectre and the Phantom Stranger not gotten involved, he might never have learned the truth at all. Batman decides not to take vengeance on him, but then Chill isconvenientlycrushed by some falling debris anyhow. Not that the Spectre would know anything about that...

characters.name: Kalibak
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Darkseid's oldest son and the leader of the forces of Apokalips. Adaptational Badass: Most incarnations of Kalibak tend to be little more than aJobberto Superman. This Kalibak, meanwhile, is the most threatening incarnation of the character to date, having defeated the entire Justice League single-handedly (which Superman was admittedly not a part of yet). Composite Character: Steppenwolf's role as Darkseid'sFrontline Generalwas given to Kalibak here. The Dragon: To his father, Darkseid. Hero Killer:Subverted. The teaser for "The Knights of Tomorrow!" shows The Question seemingly jumping to his death to escape Kalibak. "Darkseid Descending!" shows that he survived.

characters.name: Kite Man
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: The former boss of Eel O'Brien in his criminal days, Kite Man is a crazed maniac obsessed with kites and Benjamin Franklin due to a childhood incident. His two desires are to be the most famous kite-related person ever, and to get revenge on O'Brien. Adaptational Badass: He gets his own group of henchmen, who all share his gimmick of using kites to glide around, and is also shown to be anEvil Geniuswho invents a device that can remove the elasticity of whatever it hits, alongside having his ownDragonin the form of Rubberneck. He even directly fights Batman and Plastic Man after both he and the Caped Crusader temporarily gain Plas'sRubber Manpowers, and immediately adapts to them! Adaptational Seriousness. The usually silly andincompetentKite Man has now become a cold and vengeful madman who pulls off an impressive revenge scheme on Plastic Man. Arch-Enemy: For Plastic Man. Fittingly, Plastic Man's arch-nemesis is every bit as ridiculous as the rest of his life. Broken Pedestal: He used to idolize Ben Franklin, but now considers him a fraud after the incident that gave him his kite obsession (he tried recreating Franklin's famous kite experiment, got zapped and went crazy).

characters.name: K'rull the Eternal
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A Neanderthal man who gained immortality from the strange light of a glowing red meteor, K'rull believes himself to be intrinsically superior to the mere humans who now rule the globe. He lives for the day when he can overthrowHomo sapiensand take his rightful place as ruler...and don't let his caveman look fool you, because he's more than smart enough to do it. Amazon Chaser: He likes how his henchwoman becomes more muscular. Composite Character: Of Captain Marvel villain King Kull and Vandal Savage, with a hint of Darkseid's son Kalibak (though that might just be from being voiced by Michael Dorn). Genius Bruiser: Several thousand years have given him a lot of time to get some reading in. Though it doesn't mean he can't enjoy the fun side of particle colliders - smashing things into walls. Green Rocks: He got his immortality from a red meteorite.

characters.name: Lew Moxxon
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A former high-ranking crime lord in Gotham when Bruce Wayne was a child, now elderly and infirm, but holding information the Dark Knight seeks. Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: In-between mentioning all the legit criminal deeds he performed over the decades, he idly mentions he also once yelled at his wife. Dies Differently in Adaptation: Comic Moxxon got hit by a truck running from Batman. Here, he instead dies in a hospital bed. Disproportionate Retribution: Thomas Wayne thwarted his robbery attempt, so he decides to send a hitman to whack him. This turns out to be an extremely bad decision. Even Evil Has Standards: He was very specific to Joe Chill thatonlyThomas Wayne should be killed, if he was going to do it, and to at least make it look like an accident. He feels bad that Joe's screw-up left Bruce without a mom.

characters.name: Morgaine le Fay
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Medieval witch. Arthur's sister.You may have heard of her.Enslaved Etrigan in Arthurian times to help take over Camelot and kill Merlin. Adaptational Attractiveness: The comic version of Morgaine (as well as her counterpart in theJustice Leaguecartoon) has to wear a mask and armor to hide her hideously decayed face. In this show, she's downright gorgeous.Justifiedsince this is supposed to be during her early years. Cain and Abel: She's the Cain to Arthur's Abel, overthrowing his kingdom. Composite Character: She takes on a bit of Nimue, Merlin's student who betrayed him. Evil Brit: Fitting since she is a figure of Arthurian legend.

characters.name: Mr. Mind
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Batman Gambit: He constructs a ray that he tells everyone is a Death ray, and anticipates Dr. Sivana betraying him and using it on him. So he intentionally made it a Growth Ray that turns him into a monster. Big Creepy-Crawlies: He uses the growth ray to turn himself into one. Big "NO!": He does not take well to being defeated by a baby. Bond Villain Stupidity: A fairly tame version. He cannot help taunt the Baby Batman after all signs show he is completley helpess to defend himself, but given it's Batman he still had a trick up his sleeve. The Chessmaster: Masterminds taking over the Monster Society, turning the Marvels against one another, tricking the villains to building a growth ray for him, and even anticipates Sivana betraying him and using said ray on him which wasAll According to Plan.

characters.name: Mrs. Manface
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Manfreda Donatella Face is the wife of Babyface. She has the face of a square-jawed man (complete with a five o'clock shadow), but the voice and body of a normal woman. Battle Couple: With Babyface. Butter Face: It's all in the name. She has the body of a classic dame but the face of a square-jawed man with five o'clock shadow. Canon Foreigner: Like Babyface she was created specifically for the show. Lady Looks Like a Dude: She's meant to look like a cross-dressing man.

characters.name: The Music Meister
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Picked on at school for being in choir, he eventually discovered that he could control people's minds using his singing voice. What results is quite possibly the greatestMusical Episodeof anything ever. Beware the Silly Ones: He fully embraces his ability to control others by singing and is one of the campiest characters in an already incredibly campy cartoon, but he manages to nearly take over the entire planet Earth, and repeatedly successfully fends off Batman himself without a hitch. Breakout Villain: Despite being aOne-Shot Character, he's become one of the most well-known characters fromBrave and the Bold, enough to give him a silent cameo in the ending of the series, as well as show up in other DC properties, being a guest character in theArrowverse(albeitheavily reworked), and becoming a playable character in theLEGO Batman Seriesvideo game series starting with3. In 2022, he was finallyfolded into the comicsas part of theDC Pridelineup. Camp Straight: He has a musical theme,Unlimited Wardrobeof ostentatious outfits, an openly gay voice actor—and aVillainous Crushon Black Canary. Canon Immigrant:DC Pride2022brought him into the comics, wherehe was given the civilian name of "Darius Chapel", though before that, he did end up as a villain onArrowverse'sSupergirl (2015)andThe Flash (2014).

characters.name: Ocean Master
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: AQUAMAN's half-brother, who has had to live in his brother's shadow ever since their mother made Arthur king of Atlantis. He used to be a villain, but has now gotten over that. Really... Adaptational Heroism: While he's still a scheming fiend out to take over Atlantis, he's often depicted as straightforward evil,especiallyinJustice League. This version genuinely cares about his homeland, to the point where he teams up with Arthur to save it from Black Manta. Adaptational Ugliness: Comic Orm is conventionally attractive. This guy's been hit with an ugly stick, just so we know he's clearly bad news. Cain and Abel: To AQUAMAN. Even Evil Has Standards: He wants to rule Atlantis, notdestroy itlike Black Manta does.

characters.name: Per Degaton
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A Germanic mad scientist who once fought the JSA, long ago, going missing when the first Black Canary damaged his equipment, only returning in the modern day and age thanks to a loyal flunky. Badass Normal: Has no superpowers, but still overpowers the Justice Society as soon as he's released, and even has Batman's number in a fistfight. Composite Character: He takes over Hitler's role of the Spear of Destiny's wielder from the comics. Curb-Stomp Battle: Delivers one to Wildcat. Faux Affably Evil: He greets Wildcat as if he were an old friend, but it's clear that it's nothing but sardonic, and he calls him a weak old relic.

characters.name: The Planet Master
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A supervillain with the power of all the planets of the Solar System (and yes, that includes Pluto). Achievements in Ignorance: Despite Pluto not being a planet, he is still able to use its powers. Berserk Button: Don't mention Pluto's status as a dwarf planet. He's sensitive.Blue Beetle:News flash: Pluto isn't considered a planet anymore.Planet Master:INSOLENCE! Chest Insignia: It changes to match the planet he's channeling the power of. Dishing Out Dirt: Saturn's power gives him the ability to move rocks with his mind. He uses them to make a rock buzzsaw.

characters.name: Poison Ivy
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Known by her real name Pamela Isley, Poison Ivy's work deals with flowers and all things plant, including a giant venus flytrap named Georgia that she once fed Batman to because he refused to marry her. Affably Evil: To help balance out herFiery Redheadtemperament. Amazon Brigade: The Flower Children, who follow her orders. Ambiguously Bi: HerAmazon Brigadewith her Flower Children and the fact that she leads an all-female team (and her friendship with Harley Quinn) could be hinting at signs of being interested in women. Although, she does seem interested in making Batman her mate. Beauty Is Bad: This trope goes without saying.

characters.name: Professor Zee
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: The assistant to Per Degaton, still devoted to serving his master long after his disappearance. Composite Character: In the comics, Professor Zee was a victim of Degaton's whom he stole his time machine from. The Dragon: For Per Degaton. Gadgeteer Genius: Anticipating Degaton would want an army when he was restored, Zee went ahead and built him a new one. I Was Quite a Looker: He used to have a full head of hair, a thick, square jawline like a bucket, and a muscular build, but by the time of the present, he's become a decrepit old man with crooked teeth that has only a few strands of hair left and a hunchback.

characters.name: Professor Zoom
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: The yellow-cladEvil Counterpartto the Flash, Eobard Thawne is a criminal who hails from the 25th century. His mission is to destroy his lawful nemesis and all that the Flash stands for. Adaptational Nice Guy: Believe it or not, this adaptation of Eobard Thawne actually manages to be one of the least nasty versions of the character yet. Unlike the comics version or theDCAMU versionwho are notoriousSerial Killerswilling tocause rampant damage to history via time travel abuse, this Thawne has no directly stated bodycount and has the more tamer goal of ruling the future as his own kingdom. Sure he traps Barry to siphon off his speed, but that's still far less awful compared to the level of torment other Thawnes have put Barry through. Arch-Enemy: To the Flash, specifically Barry Allen. Casting Gag: Eobard Thawne theArch-Enemyof Barry Allen, is nowplayed by Barry Allen himself. The Chessmaster: He successfully manipulates Barry Allen to be trapped in the future to be used as a power source, allowing him to take over the 25th century as anEvil Overlord.

characters.name: Psycho-Pirate
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Gaining powers off of others' fears, Psycho Pirate lures his victims into traps that will leave them reliving their worst nightmares so he may feed off of pure fear. Adaptational Jerkass: A much eviller version of Psycho Pirate. The comics version never resorted to prolongedMind Rape. Adapted Out: No mention of his Medusa Mask is made. Does This Remind You of Anything?: There are some disturbing ephebophilic undertones to his torment of The Outsiders, as he literally kidnapped a group of minors, held them against their will in a secluded location, and exploits them in a way that causes them great distress and trauma.He even licks his lipsas he enjoys their emotional pain. Emotion Eater: He feeds on anger, which is why he tries to put his victims in situations instigating rage.

characters.name: Punch & Jewelee
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A pair of acrobatic, clown-themed criminals. In a Single Bound: Jewelee manages to jump high enough and far enough to land on Punch's back while he's still moving. Villainous Harlequin: Their motif. The Voiceless: They never say a word in "Menace of the Conqueror Caveman".

characters.name: Rohtul
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A m-geniusscientist on the planet Zur-En-Arrh, and arch-enemy of that world' Batman, the short-tempered Rohtul is determined to show the whole world how great his mind is, by stomping it flat. Just after he gets rid of that meddling Batman, first. Actor Allusion: As he is voiced by the very same man who once voiced the DCAU's Lex Luthor, this trope naturally goes without saying. Adaptational Backstory Change: In the comics he is a distant descendant of Lex Luthor, rather thanIdentical Strangeralien he is here. Awesomeness by Analysis: Manages to work out how to disable Batman's powers, simply by deducing his likely point of origin. Bald of Evil: He's based on Luthor after all, so of course he'd be a bald bad guy.

characters.name: Rubberneck
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: An adversary of Plastic Man's, this latex leviathan may not be very bright, but his rubbery nature makes actually knocking him down a difficult prospect. The Brute: He's strong and extremely durable, thanks to his rubbery physiology protecting him from most attacks, but doesn't have much going on upstairs. Canon Foreigner: Has no counterpart in the comics. The Dragon: He works for Kite Man. Dumbass Has a Point: When his boss sarcastically asks what Benjamin Franklin ever contributed to society, his answer is "Daylight Savings Time", which actually was a concept Benjamin Franklin originally proposed.

characters.name: Ruby Ryder
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: A hostage turned partner in crime to Cavalier, Ruby Rider first appears in the episode "Bold Beginnings!" during Green Arrow's story segment. Bait-and-Switch: She does this to Batman and Green Arrow after Cavalier appears and her true colors are revealed. Shortly after that, her and Cavalier tie Batman and Green Arrow to a stake as Cavalier tosses a torch at the logs before making his getaway but not before mocking Batman and Green Arrow by calling them the charred crusader and burnt bowman respectively. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She puts on this act to get Batman and Green Arrow to save her, only to reveal she didn't need saving and that she was Cavalier's partner in crime all along. Disproportionate Retribution: Much like her partner in crime Cavalier, she too has no problem with leaving Batman and Green Arrow for dead. Evil Cannot Comprehend Good: It's only after her actual intentions are revealed that this starts to become obvious to Green Arrow and Batman.

characters.name: Scarecrow
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Evil Sounds Deep: This Scarecrow is given a deep gravelly almost demonic sounding voice. Lean and Mean: Just like the Riddler, The Weeper, and Gentleman Ghost, Scarecrow is skinny compared to most of Batman's foes. Mind Rape: HisEvil Planin "Trials of the Demon" is to lace Jack o' Lanterns around with Fear Gas so that when all the kids celebrate Halloween they will be wallowing in fear. Sinister Scythe: He wields a scythe in direct combat to go with his gimmick. Supernatural Fear Inducer: A staple of Scarecrow is his Fear Gas that makes his victims see everything transformed into monstrous forms.

characters.name: Sinestro
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: The Green Lantern of Sector 1417, considered the most peaceful of all sectors in the known universe. However, during the fight against Despero, Sinestro shows his true colors when he turns against the Corps. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He initially seems like just another Green Lantern, even allowing Batman to assist when Guy tells him to get lost. Then it turns out that he took over his own world, and decides to kill Mogo as plan A. While beating up Guy, he even declares he thought himself better than the other lanterns. Evil Cannot Comprehend Good: Ultimately, the reason he is a villain is because he refuses to put his faith in other people. He attempts to kill Mogo because he doesn't understand what Batman sees in G'nort that would leave him to entrust G'nort with his plan to stop Despero. Faux Affably Evil: He acts like a sophisticated gentleman which even manages to fool Batman, while secretly he's just as bad as Despero. Knight Templar: He believes in order at all costs, to the extent of enslaving his own sector to ensure that no conflict arose from it.

characters.name: Slug
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Body Horror: A fall into a vat of chemicals makes him even more unsightly to look at, and adds tentacles growing from random places. Canon Foreigner: Created exclusively for the show, though he does share similarities to New God Sleez. Gonk: Fat, pale and ugly. It's one of the things Wildcat taunts him about.

characters.name: Sportsmaster
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: No True Scotsman: Proclaims that bowling isn't a sport when he crashes a bowling tournament. Unholy Matrimony: Married to the Tigress, with a pre-teen daughter, also a supervillain. Villains Out Shopping: AQUAMAN spots him driving down a freeway while on vacation. His glee at the thought of a potential plot to thwart is dashed when he sees Sportsmaster is also on vacation with his wife and daughter... and from the looks of it, they're having about as much fun as AQUAMAN'S having on his.

characters.name: Steppenwolf
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Mongul's champion in his Gladiator tournaments. Adaptational Dumbass: Steppenwolf is typically a lieutenant or commander for Darkseid, while here he is relegated to just being the muscle. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In the comics, he was Darkseid's lackey, his uncle no less. Here he instead works for Mongul. The Dragon: For Mongul, being his Gladiator champion. You Have Failed Me: After losing Mongul's death-race, he's zapped, and told he's no longer Mongul's champion.

characters.name: Takeo
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In the comics, Takeo's motive was toMurder the Hypotenuse, his brother Makeo, for marrying Katana. Since Katana is de-aged to a teenager, Makeo isAdapted Out, and Takeo instead kills Katana’s mentor Tadashi. Ambiguous Situation: His appearance is only in Katana's memories, fueled by guilt being egged on by Psycho-Pirate, and Batman claims she's misremembering what went down. Karma Houdini: Katana's flashback never specifies if she managed to avenge her master's death at his hands.

characters.name: The Terrible Trio
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Fox, Shark, and Vulture are bored millionaires who become martial artists that wear masks of the animals they represent. As members of the Shadow Clan, they plan to steal the Wudang Totem from its respective temple. Adaptational Badass: This version of the Trio are skilled martial artists who trained alongside Batman and Bronze Tiger. Adaptational Nice Guy: Compared to his incarnation inThe Animated Series, Fox seems to be less condescending, to the point he only looks down upon Tiger not because he's not from a wealthy background, butbecause he has a big ego. He even (allegedly) promises to leave Tiger's village alone if he swallows his pride and bow before him. Adaptation Origin Connection: "Return of the Fearsome Fangs!" has flashbacks that depict them training alongside Batman and Bronze Tiger prior to Bruce Wayne becoming Batman. While Bruce and Ben Turner are martial artist in the comics, the Trio aren't and Bruce and Ben didn't train together. Arrogant Kung-Fu Guy: They are all pretty stuck-up due to their powers, especially Fox.

characters.name: Tornado Champion / Tornado Tyrant
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: Big Ol' Eyebrows: As the Tyrant, he gains a pair of large eyebrows that go beyond his head. Blow You Away: Same as Red Tornado, he generates bursts of wind. Crazy-Prepared: Red Tornado built in a failsafe system just in case.Champion saw this coming, and had it removed. Easily Condemned: It takes precisely one tantrum for Batman to declare Champion is utterly irredeemable and needs to be destroyed forever. Fantastic Racism: On the giving and receiving end.Giving: He's not impressed with Batman even before he gets emotions, dismissing him as an organic lifeform. He gets worse once he gets emotions.Receiving: Police get hostile with him just for being a robot.

characters.name: The Weeper
characters.media_title: Batman: The Brave and the Bold
characters.description: An elderly has-been supervillain who originally terrorised Bulletman. After botching his big opportunity to completely destroy Fawcett City many decades ago, he served hard time and retired completely from all criminality... at least, until the Joker discovered him and vowed to help bring him back into the villain game. Adaptational Nice Guy: The Weeper of the comics would never have hesitated to commit mass murder. Becoming the Mask: He admits that his mewls were originally part of the gimmick, but ever since his biggest plan was foiled by his own split second of hesitation, he's just shed "bitter tears of regret". Catchphrase: "How sad it is". Composite Character: He's a combination of his regular self (whose only ties to the Joker were his son andsuccessorworking with him under the orders of King Kull in the Bronze AgeJustice League of Americastory "Crisis on Earth-S") and Willy the Weeper, a criminal the Joker formed an alliance with and helped overcome a habit of bursting into tears while committing crimes in the second issue ofhis short-lived ongoing series from the 1970s.
